claims.text: Advanced computational modeling and machine-learning algorithms are proposed as the single intervention.
The intervention can determine melting temperature in high-entropy alloys.
The intervention can determine enthalpy and entropy of fusion in high-entropy alloys.
The intervention can determine volume change upon melting in high-entropy alloys.
The intervention can determine liquid thermodynamic properties in high-entropy alloys.
Machine learning can handle the complex data associated with high-entropy alloys.
Computational power and machine learning can overcome limitations in the accuracy of thermodynamic-property determination.
Computational power and machine learning can overcome limitations in the availability of thermodynamic-property determinations.
Computational power and machine learning can overcome limitations in the efficiency of thermodynamic-property determination.
The intervention will improve accuracy relative to current experimental and computational methods.
The intervention will improve efficiency relative to current experimental and computational methods.
The proposed approach applies to high-entropy-alloy compositions representable by existing computational models.
The proposed approach applies within temperature ranges where the computational models are valid.
Performance is limited by the complexity of high-entropy alloys.
Performance is limited by computational-model accuracy.
Performance is limited by the availability of training data.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparison with independent experimental reference data for well-characterized high-entropy alloys.
